A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TADSR. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original TADSR benchmark results, component and blurred-MSE ablations, timestep analyses, and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds mapping-hyperparameter experiments, measured efficiency comparisons, and 2K-resolution examples.

M1.justification: The time-aware encoder, student–teacher timestep mapping, TAVSD objective, and blurred-MSE plus LPIPS reconstruction loss remain unchanged. Newly specified prompt extraction, timestep sampling and default hyperparameters document implementation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: v3 adds four 2K-resolution examples covering synthetic and real degradations in Section 10 and Figure 12, extending evaluation beyond the original cropped-image setting. LSDIR training and the DIV2K-Val, DRealSR, RealSR and RealLR200 benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Matched benchmark comparisons retain the same nine diffusion baselines; GAN comparisons retain BSRGAN, RealESRGAN and LDL. Existing visual comparisons retain their comparator membership. The new efficiency and high-resolution experiments use previously evaluated diffusion methods.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a five-setting mapping-hyperparameter experiment on RealSR at ts=500 and an efficiency protocol using 128×128 inputs, ×4 SR and one NVIDIA 3090 GPU. The blurred-MSE ablation drops LPIPS and MANIQA reporting. Existing benchmark splits, crops, training budgets and principal quality metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially broadens diagnostic coverage through the lambda/gamma sensitivity study in Section 7.3 and qualitative generalization tests from 512×512 training to 2K images. Table 3 also extends the existing timestep analysis with additional metrics. The original component and blurred-MSE ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained means and standard deviations in Figures 3–4 describe latent features and VSD guidance rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds mapping-sensitivity results, additional timestep metrics, efficiency measurements, and high-resolution qualitative findings, while revising GAN examples. Table 7 newly reports TADSR at 0.1465 seconds and OSEDiff at 0.1463 seconds. Matched benchmark, component-ablation and GAN scores are retained except the TSDSR RealSR SSIM correction from '6886' to 0.6886. Table 4 removes LPIPS and MANIQA entries; there is no improvement in retained TADSR benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit stop-gradient squared-loss surrogate for VSD in Equation 3 and specifies its gradient paths. This is a limited formal addition; the underlying diffusion relation and supplementary noise-to-latent residual derivation remain unchanged, with no new theorem or guarantee.

C1.justification: Both versions claim efficient single-step Real-ISR, state-of-the-art performance, and timestep-controlled fidelity–realism trade-offs through TAE and TAVSD. The new introduction contribution bullets restate these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of how teacher–LoRA residuals supply high-frequency detail and why directly noising student latents would harm fidelity. It also interprets mapping-hyperparameter sensitivity, motivates the default settings, and discusses comparable cost to OSEDiff and applicability to 2K images.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies lambda=0.5, gamma=0, DAPE prompt extraction, uniform student timestep sampling, and random timestep sampling in the ablation baseline. It documents timing hardware and replaces v1's project-page pointer with an explicit source-code release statement and repository link.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to LoRA, OMGSR, ResShift and Arbitrary-Steps Image Super-Resolution via Diffusion Inversion. It further relates TAE to timestep conditioning in StableSR, SeeSR and DiffBIR, while retaining the main research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially reorganized around two explicit shortcomings and contribution bullets. VSD background and the encoder/distillation explanations are expanded and rewritten. The supplement is reorganized into Sections 6–10 with grouped ablation subsections, alongside language and author-header corrections.

P2.justification: v3 reformats the document throughout, including a two-column supplement, and adds timestep, sensitivity and efficiency tables plus Figure 12. It removes columns from the blurred-MSE table and revises the GAN montage, adding bird and portrait examples while removing the brick example. Retained figures are resized, recropped or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through explicit mapping defaults and prompt extraction details, and strengthens evidence for controllability and efficiency with Tables 5 and 7. These benefits outweigh limited reporting weaknesses: the blurred-MSE ablation loses two metrics, and Section 7.3 overgeneralizes gamma's effect on no-reference metrics relative to Table 5. Overall, the existing study becomes clearer and better supported.
